take_homes: You can't hand someone your agent. You share context, a skill, the output or an interface, and I pick by what the person's job needs.
Check whether anyone wants the thing before I build it for the sales team. Talk to one person first.
Write the people plan with names in it. Mine usually has none, and the question of who answers for it is the real handover.

monday.move: Ask one person in sales how they do their weekly pipeline review today, and don't build anything first
monday.who: one sales lead, probably the one who sits next to me
monday.stop_condition: If they say what they have works fine or they have no time, I drop the sales setup
monday.blocker: I'll want to build the thing over the weekend instead of asking, and I haven't worked out who would maintain it

misconception.why: The module never made me check agent output, it was about adoption. It did shake my habit of building org-wide setups nobody asked for (scar story, 'what would have to be true'), but I still think checking is for beginners.

one_line: Good for the non-engineer rollout problem, and the value-stream story is real. The exercises are slow, and I'd have skipped half the checks, which proves the point of them.
